narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 59% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, that is just over a coin-flip chance of repayment difficulty, and it is above the bank’s approval cutoff, so the application did not pass.

The strongest factor increasing the risk estimate was your checking-account status: a balance in the 0–200 DM range. Among approved applicants, no checking account is much more common (59.2%) and this range is only 18.4%, so the model treated it as a warning sign. The second most influential factor was your credit history, marked as critical/other credits. Although this is not a clean record, it actually worked in your favor in this decision—it pushed the estimate toward good credit rather than toward denial. The third factor, having another bank installment plan, pushed toward bad credit; only 8.7% of approved applicants have this, versus 87.4% with none.

To improve future chances, focus on strengthening your checking-account position, avoid overdrafts or low balances, and reduce existing installment obligations before reapplying. A smaller requested amount or a revised repayment plan could also help, but the clearest next step is to address the two factors that increased your risk estimate.
